question.problem: A tank is being filled with water. What is an appropriate unit for measuring the rate of change of water volume in the tank, as time goes on?
question.worked_solution:
We *measure the change* of the volume as *we change* the amount of time. Consequently, any appropriate unit for measuring the rate of change of water volume in the tank must take the form

$$
\dfrac{\textrm{unit of volume}}{\textrm{unit of time}}.
$$

Some examples of appropriate units include $\dfrac{\textrm{liters}}{\textrm{hour}},$ $\dfrac{\textrm{m}^3}{\textrm{min}},$ and $\dfrac{\textrm{cm}^3}{\textrm{s}}.$
